title: upper back (thoracic region)

chart.description: The back from the base of the neck to the twelfth thoracic vertebra, unrolled round a horizontal section of the skin. u: arc length (cm) from the posterior median line, positive towards the patient's LEFT. v: height (cm) above the tip of the C7 spinous process (negative below it). d: depth below the skin along the inward normal (cm).

structures.label: spinal cord in its dural sac

description: Over the thoracic spine the skin, subcutaneous fat, trapezius, rhomboids and the erector spinae cover the laminae and transverse processes; lateral to them the ribs and intercostal spaces lie over the pleura and lung, which are reached at a few centimetres in a slim patient. The scapula covers the upper lateral back with the arms at the sides. In the midline, between the spinous processes, the ligaments lead to the spinal canal and the spinal cord. Points of the inner and outer bladder lines are needled obliquely towards the spine.

review.notes: Depths below the skin of the lungs, organs, bones and great vessels are measured on one reference body (a 38-year-old man of about 90 kg) and scaled to each patient by height and BMI; the rest is schematic. Not a guide to safe depths in real patients. Anatomical expert review is required before any teaching use.

provenance.notes: Depth grid (2 cm): depths of the lungs, vertebrae, kidneys and spinal cord measured by rays on the reference body; the fat/muscle split, the ribs (not modelled: treated as intercostal spaces) and the scapula (a schematic bony plate) are schematic. Midline zones lead through the interspinous ligaments to the spinal canal (critical).
